clue.text: Reserve team follows out east

indicators.note: follows places the team word after the scrambled letters
out signals that the letters of the word east are put out of order

parts.note: a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A reserve team trails some opponents from out east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like away, but it is the anagram signal on 'east'; 'follows' puts the team after the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside money is to reserve it, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Percussion played very fast

indicators.note: played means the letters of the word are performed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Drums performed at a breakneck tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: Faster than the speed of sound, so extremely fast.

clue.text: Would he have skill raising end of mast?

definitions.text: Would he have skill raising end of mast?

indicators.note: in a down entry the final letter is lifted to the top

parts.note: art is skill

explanation.surface: Who has the knack of climbing to the masthead?
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising end' moves the T of ART to the top, and T is also the end of 'mast'. A sailor is the one with the skill to climb it.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack tar is a sailor, someone with the skill to scale rigging.

clue.text: Broke, so went halves to secure drug

indicators.note: securing means holding the drug inside

parts.note: to go halves is to share
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Penniless, so two people split the cost of some drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke' looks like poor; it is the verb meaning snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sheared has broken off under a cutting or twisting force.

clue.text: Order prosecution for sabotage?

parts.note: to direct is to order
an action is a legal proceeding

explanation.surface: Ordering a prosecution for wrecking equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks sabotage as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Militant protest such as strikes or wrecking is example of the campaign tactic.

clue.text: Adder with wiry frame and beady look

definitions.text: Adder with wiry frame and beady look

parts.words: Adder with wiry frame and beady look
parts.note: not a snake but something that adds up: a counting device of beads strung on wires in a frame

explanation.surface: A thin, beady-eyed snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead frame on wires is the old calculating device, so it is literally an adder of numbers.

clue.text: Well-weighted rod picked up by sportsman

definitions.text: Well-weighted rod picked up by sportsman

parts.words: Well-weighted rod picked up by sportsman
parts.note: suggests an angler's rod, but it is a weighted bar a weightlifter lifts

explanation.surface: A fishing rod with good balance chosen by an angler.
explanation.definitionFit: The weightlifter's bar carries heavy discs at each end and is lifted overhead.

clue.text: Financial officer's representative, in bed, put on bandage

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: put on places the bandage after, under it in a down entry
in puts the representative inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
MP is a Member of Parliament
a roller is a rolled bandage

explanation.surface: An official's deputy, laid up in bed, has had a dressing applied.
explanation.definitionFit: A comptroller is a controller of accounts, the title of some financial officials.

clue.text: Sure to miss a stroke finally in breaking waves

indicators.note: the final letter loses one stroke of its shape, the bottom bar of an E leaving an F

explanation.surface: Certain to fluff a swimming stroke at last in the breakers.
explanation.walkthrough: A capital E without its bottom stroke is an F.
explanation.definitionFit: Surf is the foaming water of waves breaking on the shore.

clue.text: Almost slipped behind separate area of garden

indicators.note: behind places the shortened word after the other piece

parts.note: to separate is to part

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short of its final letter

parts.note: to slip is to err, so slipped is erred

explanation.surface: Someone nearly fell behind in a separate part of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims the final letter of the synonym for slipped; 'behind' places that after the word for separate.
explanation.definitionFit: A parterre is a formal ornamental garden section laid out in beds.

clue.text: At hour of prayer, beginning to read instructive book

parts.note: prime is the canonical office said at the first hour of the day

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the first letter of the word read

explanation.surface: At morning prayers someone starts reading an improving book.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIME is one of the canonical hours of monastic prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A primer is an elementary textbook teaching the basics of a subject.

clue.text: The influence of the Lords that whips people into line?

definitions.text: The influence of the Lords that whips people into line?

parts.words: The influence of the Lords that whips people into line?
parts.note: read as the pressure exerted by members of the House of Lords, it is really the push of one's equals to conform

explanation.surface: Upper-house pressure that keeps members obedient to the whips.
explanation.definitionFit: Social pressure from one's equals is what pushes people to conform.

clue.text: Censure for revolutionary folk — time for resumption of friendly relations

parts.note: a rap is a rebuke
pro means in favour of
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary
men means people

explanation.surface: A rebuke to revolutionary types, then a call to make up and be friends again.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'for' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapprochement is the restoring of harmonious relations, especially between nations.

clue.text: Split up platoon?

definitions.meaning: a platoon is literally a section of an army company

explanation.surface: A platoon divided.
explanation.definitionFit: To go separate ways, and whimsically a section of a military company.

clue.text: Simple manoeuvres alert enemy

indicators.note: manoeuvres means the letters are moved about into a new position

explanation.surface: Easy tactics keep the foe on their toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means basic, easy and simple.

clue.text: Provided with motive power, rose effortlessly, just after the start

indicators.note: the word is taken from just after its start, so its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to soar is to rise high effortlessly

explanation.surface: Something powered rose easily just after setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just after the start' removes the S from SOARED.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat is oared when propelled by oars, which supply its motive power.

clue.text: One taken in by girl that's sweet

parts.note: April is a girl's name
a fool is a British dessert of puréed fruit folded into cream

explanation.surface: A girl's sweetheart has been deceived.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a cold British pudding of fruit and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tricked by a prank on 1 April is the victim, a person duped or taken in.

clue.text: Place of growing culture in island coming to peak

parts.note: taken as written
Cuba is a Caribbean island
a tor is a rocky hilltop

explanation.surface: Somewhere culture is growing on an island reaching its peak.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hill on English moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacterial cultures are grown in a warm cabinet kept at constant temperature.

clue.text: Touch-type?

parts.note: not keyboard skill without looking, but a kind of type read by touch

explanation.surface: Typing by touch.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised-dot writing system for blind readers is read by fingertip.

clue.text: Officer's drinking beer in US city

indicators.note: drinking means the officer takes the beer inside

parts.note: SM is a sergeant major
ale is beer

explanation.surface: An officer drinks beer in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Salem in Massachusetts is the American town of the witch trials.

clue.text: Travels to game abroad

parts.note: journeys overseas to see wild animals, game being big wildlife rather than a match

explanation.surface: Going overseas to watch a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Expeditions in Africa to view or hunt wild animals.

clue.text: Naked ladies and intoxicating drink — ouch, the stigma!

parts.note: mead is fermented honey
ow is a cry of pain
saffron is the dried stigma of a crocus

explanation.surface: Nude women, strong drink and a cry of shame at the disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stigma' is not disgrace but the flower part; 'Naked ladies' is a folk name for the plant, which flowers leafless.
explanation.definitionFit: The autumn crocus-like plant Colchicum is popularly called naked ladies because its flowers rise without leaves.

clue.text: Church members go bankrupt, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a congregation, a flock in a pen

explanation.surface: Churchgoers who go broke.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen for sheep, hence a congregation; and to cease trading.

clue.text: How one speaks finally to mass meeting

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word to

parts.note: a rally is a large gathering

explanation.surface: How a speaker finally addresses a big gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking is done by mouth, so the adverb meaning by word of mouth fits.

clue.text: Dishonourable money — it's rejected by a raped girl

parts.note: filthy lucre is ill-gotten money

indicators.note: rejected means the word it is turned back

parts.note: it, with the 's linking

explanation.surface: Dirty money is turned down by a girl who has been wronged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns IT into TI. Lucretia, in Roman legend, was raped by Tarquin's son.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman legend the virtuous Lucretia was violated by Sextus Tarquinius, prompting the monarchy's fall.

clue.text: Modest amount that starts off the American Dream

indicators.note: starts off picks out the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A small sum to kick-start the American Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A tad is a small amount or a little bit.

clue.text: Poet was lost for words, an audience heard

indicators.note: what an audience hears signals the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: an actor who forgets lines has dried, followed by an

explanation.surface: A poet who forgot his lines in front of a listening crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: An actor 'dries' when lines are forgotten; 'dried an' said aloud gives the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was the English Restoration poet and first Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Sad fate recollected at start of yearly celebration

indicators.note: recollected read as re-collected means the letters are gathered up again in a new order
at start of takes the first letter of the word yearly

explanation.surface: A sad event recalled at the start of an annual celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' rearranges SADFATE into FEASTDA, and Y comes from 'yearly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A feast day is a religious festival, a day of celebration in the calendar.
